reason: Base UI draws Checkbox and Radio as a span, so shadcn's disabled:opacity-50 (a :disabled selector) never matches and a disabled control stays fully opaque upstream; lyra reads [data-disabled] instead, which is what the utility means. An upstream defect, not a lyra value. Same as foundation's.

The preset is generated with rtl:false, so its paddings and radii are physical (pl-/pr-) and do not mirror under dir=rtl; the layer-3 rules are logical. The section proves DirectionProvider renders, not a value. Same as foundation's.

A preset app's globals.css carries no .cn-* rules, so the cn-input-otp class the shadcn component keeps is unstyled there; style-lyra.css's `.cn-input-otp { gap-2 }` is lyra's own value and the system keeps it. Same as foundation's.

The shortcuts contain ⌘, which is in no JetBrains Mono build: the reference app falls back through next/font's "JetBrains Mono Fallback" and the preview through the Pretendard Hangul fallback, so the glyph advance differs. Measured here at 4.3–20.3px, an order of magnitude wider than the ~0.5px foundation sees in Inter — a monospace body font makes the one non-monospace glyph on the row the whole difference, and the menubar row (20.3px) is the worst case because it carries the longest shortcut. Font stack, not a value.

lyra's generated questionnaire.tsx carries `sm:min-h-8` on QuestionnaireActions while the shadcn base component (which registry/ui follows) carries `sm:min-h-9`. The preset bakes the value into the component as a utility, so no layer-3 rule can reach it and one shared set of TSX cannot hold both. The row and everything it stretches are 4px taller here. Same shape as foundation's, with lyra's number.

Dark mode only: Tailwind sorts lyra's dark: colours (dark:bg-input/30 on the outline button, dark:border-input, dark:aria-invalid:border-destructive/50 on the checkbox) after the state utilities that have no dark counterpart (aria-expanded:bg-muted, aria-invalid:aria-checked:border-primary), so upstream an open outline trigger, an alert-dialog cancel button and an invalid checked checkbox lose their state colour in dark. lyra keeps the state colours; reproducing the ordering would delete the signal. Same as foundation's.
